item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: March 26, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Major Housing and Land Use Reforms:** Council will consider significant changes to city zoning rules, including allowing more diverse housing types like townhomes and small multi-unit buildings ("missing middle housing"), establishing maximum parking requirements for new developments, and expanding opportunities for home-based businesses (e.g., Accessory Commercial Units). * **New City-Wide Transportation Plan:** A public hearing will be held to discuss and potentially adopt the "Austin Core Transportation Plan," an update to the city's strategic mobility framework. * **Addressing Homelessness:** Council will review and consider adopting the new 2025-2027 Strategic Plan, which outlines the city's comprehensive approach to tackling homelessness. * **City Boundary Adjustments:** Multiple public hearings are scheduled to consider removing several properties from the city's full-purpose jurisdiction, as mandated by state law (Senate Bill 1844). * **Billboard and Electronic Sign Regulations:** Policy discussions will take place on proposed amendments to city rules governing off-premise signs, including their relocation, allowable sizes, and electronic display options.

item.title: Austin Austin Housing Finance Corporation: March 26, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation agenda: * The Austin Housing Finance Corporation will consider authorizing a loan of up to $3.5 million to support an affordable housing project. * This funding is designated for "Sunday Village," an affordable housing development located near 1026 Clayton Lane (formerly known as Arbors at Creekside). * The decision aims to provide permanent affordable housing options for the community, utilizing funds from the corporation's Fiscal Year 2025-26 Capital Budget.

item.title: Austin Work Session: March 24, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council Work Session agenda: * **Addressing Homelessness:** Council will discuss and potentially approve a new strategic plan for 2025-2027 to guide Austin's efforts and investments in addressing homelessness. * **Major Housing Zoning Changes:** Significant amendments to city zoning rules are on the table to allow for more diverse and affordable housing options, including "missing middle" housing types like townhomes and cottage courts, and developments that mix residential and commercial uses. * **Public Hearing on Sign Regulations:** A public hearing will be held on a proposed ordinance to change sign regulations, potentially allowing for larger electronic signs and off-premises advertising in public areas. * **I-35 Cap and Stitch Project Update:** Council members will receive a briefing with recommendations regarding the ongoing I-35 Cap and Stitch infrastructure project.

item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: March 12, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Major Infrastructure Funding:** The Council will consider authorizing up to $575 million in bonds for the Water and Wastewater System and a $1 billion low-interest loan from the EPA to fund a $1.5 billion expansion of the Walnut Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant. * **Significant Land Use Decisions:** Public hearings are scheduled for numerous property rezonings across the city, including changes for commercial, mixed-use, and residential developments. The Council will also initiate the rezoning process for the 445-acre Jimmy Clay and Roy Kizer Golf Courses. * **Policy & Community Initiatives:** Items include amending city lobbyist regulations, approving economic development funding for The Vortex (a local cultural business), and advancing a mixed-use development on St. John Avenue with a focus on deeper affordability.

item.title: Austin Austin Housing Finance Corporation: March 12, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation agenda: * The **Austin Housing Finance Corporation** will consider a significant financial commitment to increase housing options in Austin. * A key item on the agenda is the proposed **approval of a loan up to $5.5 million** for a new multifamily rental development. * This funding is for "The Bloom at Lamar Square," a project located near 1326 and 1328 Lamar Square Drive, aimed at supporting **affordable rental housing**.
